item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Sat Aug 29 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Sat Aug 29, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: We the People First Friday — Fri Sep 4, 5:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Stop by the Ware Center on the Lancaster Print Crawl! This citywide interactive printing event showcases the talented design & print communities in Lancaster to help raise scholarship funds for local graphic design and printing students. While you “crawl,” enjoy the homegrown sounds of Mark and Jordan Rast, a Lancaster father-son musical duo who bring their own unique flavor to Appalachian, folk, and bluegrass music. In the Regitz Gallery, join us in celebrating the opening of Wild in the Shadows by Rob Homan. Homan’s wood sculptures—sourced from a local sawmill—can take hundreds of hours each, using a series of small gouges that are then painted in vibrant colors, bringing their intricate textures to life. Free and open to the public!

item.title: Launch Event for The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker — Thu Sep 10, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Cristin O’Keefe Aptowicz will be celebrating the release of her book The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker in conversation with Darlene Colon, President of the Christiana Historical Society and direct descendant of Ezekiel Thompson. The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker is the first narrative nonfiction account of the Christiana Resistance, and the first to unite three of the radical abolitionist communities that made it possible: the wealthy free Black elite of Philadelphia, the rural white Quakers of Pennsylvania, and the fugitives from slavery who lived, worked, and ultimately fought in both worlds. This event will take place at the Stevens & Smith Center at 13 E Vine St in Lancaster. We will be selling copies of the books at the event. To reserve a copy of the book in advance, please use the link on this event. O’Keefe Aptowicz and Colon will both be available to personalize and sign books after the discussion.
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Forensic Science with Lancaster County Parks — Tue Oct 20, 10:30 AM — Columbia
item.description:
Presentation, STEM, Tweens, Teens
Put your science knowledge and observation skills into action through hands-on explorations you will unmask the clues that today’s scientists use to solve crimes. You will be guided through important aspects of scientific investigations using the same forensic clues that detectives rely upon in their work. Looking at several aspects of forensic science, “crime scenes” will be investigated by studying finger prints, visual clues and observations and bones. The vital role of insects in the wild will also be examined as it pertains to forensic science.Ages 10 - 15.Limit 30 youth. Registration required. Youth may attend without a caregiver; however, we do ask that the caregiver remains present in the building during the program. THANK YOU, Columbia Fraternal Association for sponsoring this program.
